name: Government of the Elysian Concord
summary: Constitutional structure, rights, entrenchment tiers, planetary institutions, elections, and the independent offices.

charter.name: The Concord Charter
charter.summary: Constitution of the Elysian Concord, in force since EY-0001-M01-D01; 41,000 words in each of 41 equally authoritative languages.
charter.openingLine: We were not conquered into this. We agreed, having seen the alternative.

structuralPrinciples.name: Decentralization by default
structuralPrinciples.summary: All powers rest with Regions except those the Charter enumerates to the Concord; ambiguity resolves downward.

structuralPrinciples.name: The audit principle
structuralPrinciples.summary: Every organ of government is audited by a body it cannot appoint, fund, or discipline.

structuralPrinciples.name: Ecological limits are constitutional
structuralPrinciples.summary: Article 12 thresholds cannot be suspended by legislation, emergency, or executive act.

structuralPrinciples.name: Candour in government
structuralPrinciples.summary: Published deliberations, mandatory minority reports, and the reasons requirement.

structuralPrinciples.name: The humility clause
structuralPrinciples.summary: Where words and purposes diverge, prefer purposes; where purposes are unclear, prefer the reading that leaves most room to correct a mistake.

enumeratedPowers.name: Planetary commons
enumeratedPowers.summary: Deep ocean, polar ice, and orbital space; no Region can own them.

enumeratedPowers.name: Defence, disarmament verification, and disaster response
enumeratedPowers.summary: Direct lesson of the Long Emergency.

enumeratedPowers.name: Interregional transport, grid, and communications backbone
Constrained List materials and strategic reserves

powersNote: Everything not enumerated is regional or local. The Concord may set floors but not ceilings, and may not direct how a Region meets a floor.

rights.name: Freedom of belief and non-belief
rights.summary: No established religion, no religious test.

rights.name: Freedom of expression, association, and assembly
Freedom of movement and residence
rights.summary: No internal borders, no internal citizenship.

rights.name: Bodily and reproductive autonomy
rights.summary: The Charter expressly forbids any birth quota, incentive, or restriction.

rights.name: Freedom from torture, arbitrary detention, and capital punishment
rights.summary: Capital punishment abolished at the founding.

rights.name: Equality before the law
rights.summary: Without distinction of region, language, belief, sex, ancestry, or disability.

rights.name: Privacy of person, home, communications, and data
Housing adequate to health and dignity
Subsistence income
rights.summary: Sufficient for participation in civic life.

rights.name: Access to the commons
rights.summary: Clean air and water, and access to protected land and coast.

rights.name: Right to be governed in your own language
rights.summary: In any of the 41 registered languages.

rights.name: Right of access to record
rights.summary: Any record of any public body, with narrow, published, appealable exceptions.

rights.name: Right to reasons
rights.summary: To be told why a decision affecting you was made.

rights.name: Fair hearing, presumption of innocence, and appeal

entrenchmentTiers.name: Tier 1 — Foundational
entrenchmentTiers.summary: Rights 1-7, ecological limits, the Abolition, the amendment and withdrawal procedures.

entrenchmentTiers.name: Tier 2 — Structural
entrenchmentTiers.summary: Institutional design, distribution of competences, independent offices.

entrenchmentTiers.name: Tier 3 — Constitutional statute
entrenchmentTiers.summary: Electoral rules, procedural detail, the registered-language list.

amendmentReviewPanel.name: Amendment Review Panel
amendmentReviewPanel.summary: 300 citizens chosen by lot, sitting 90 days, taking evidence in public and publishing a non-binding reasoned opinion. No amendment may be voted on before publication.

withdrawal.name: Withdrawal procedure
withdrawal.summary: Legalised by the Fourth Amendment after the EY 31 crisis; two referendums on an absolute-majority threshold separated by a four-year cooling period, with Court-arbitrated settlement.

emergencyPowers.name: Emergency powers
emergencyPowers.summary: Real but caged; the tightest-drafted section of the Charter, written after the Emergency of EY 233.

institutions.name: The Assembly
institutions.summary: Directly elected chamber and primary legislature; 720 members on open-list proportional representation.
institutions.electoralSystem: open-list proportional representation with compensatory planetary tier

institutions.name: The Council of Regions
institutions.summary: Chamber of the constituent units and guardian of decentralization; four delegates per Region regardless of population.
institutions.absoluteVetoOn: measures touching regional competence or the distribution of powers

institutions.name: The Executive Board
institutions.summary: Collegial executive of nine; no president, no prime minister. Decisions are of the Board, not of a member.

institutions.name: The Constitutional Court
institutions.summary: Fifteen justices on single non-renewable 18-year terms, barred from all subsequent public office for life.

elections.independentExpenditure: registered, capped, published in real time
elections.recordRequirement: Every candidate publishes a standard-format record of prior positions, votes, and reversals.

commonProtections.fundingFormula: fixed proportion of planetary revenue, set constitutionally and not voted annually

offices.name: The Audit Service
offices.summary: Audits every organ of government — financial, performance, and legal compliance; may compel documents and testimony; findings trigger removal procedures.

offices.name: The Record Office
offices.summary: Administers the right of access to record and the Public Record Act; maintains the permanent archive; adjudicates access refusals.

offices.name: The Electoral Commission
offices.summary: Administers elections, registers parties, enforces campaign finance, and certifies results.

offices.name: The Ecological Commission
offices.summary: Monitors the Article 12 constitutional limits and publishes the planetary environmental account. It may measure, publish, and compel a response on breach, but cannot make policy.

offices.name: The Office of Future Generations
offices.summary: Represents Elysians not yet born; holds a one-year suspensive veto compelling a published Parliamentary response. Cannot block permanently.

nominatingAssembly.name: The Nominating Assembly
nominatingAssembly.summary: Four hundred citizens chosen by lot for one year who appoint the heads of the independent offices and confirm the Constitutional Court shortlist, and do nothing else.
nominatingAssembly.selection: sortition from the full adult population

knownWeaknesses.name: Slow amendment
knownWeaknesses.summary: Tier 1 rigidity means a genuinely necessary change could arrive too late.

knownWeaknesses.name: Court dependence
knownWeaknesses.summary: Ambiguity resolves downward because the Court says so; a captured Court could reverse decentralization.

knownWeaknesses.name: Floors without ceilings
knownWeaknesses.summary: The Concord cannot prevent a wealthy Region racing ahead, widening interregional inequality.

knownWeaknesses.name: Translation dependence
knownWeaknesses.summary: Equal authenticity of 41 texts depends on translation infrastructure.

knownWeaknesses.name: Consensus drift
knownWeaknesses.summary: A culture that prizes dissent can mistake the performance of dissent for its substance. Recognised and unsolved.

knownWeaknesses.name: Executive slowness
knownWeaknesses.summary: Collegial decision-making is slow; contributed to the Serrance Storm Failure.

knownWeaknesses.name: Council malapportionment
knownWeaknesses.summary: Veydra's 140 million hold the same Council weight as Elandris's 2.31 billion; a standing grievance.

knownWeaknesses.name: Diffuse responsibility
knownWeaknesses.summary: Collective decisions make individual blame hard to assign — sometimes a feature, sometimes an escape.

knownWeaknesses.name: Sortition variance
knownWeaknesses.summary: Nominating Assemblies vary in quality year to year and are heavily lobbied.

knownWeaknesses.name: Expertise loss
knownWeaknesses.summary: Single non-renewable terms and 10-year cooling-off discard accumulated skill by design.
